# Template in askama - Rust

Source: https://askama.rs/en/v0.14.0/doc/askama/derive.Template.html

# Derive Macro Template

```
#[derive(Template)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[template]
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`derive`## Expand description

The `Template` derive macro and its `template()` attribute.

Askama works by generating one or more trait implementations for any
`struct` type decorated with the `#[derive(Template)]` attribute. The
code generation process takes some options that can be specified through
the `template()` attribute.

[§](https://askama.rs#attributes)Attributes

The following sub-attributes are currently recognized:

[§](https://askama.rs#path)path

E.g. `path = "foo.html"`

Sets the path to the template file.
The path is interpreted as relative to the configured template directories
(by default, this is a `templates` directory next to your `Cargo.toml`).
The file name extension is used to infer an escape mode (see below). In
web framework integrations, the path’s extension may also be used to
infer the content type of the resulting response.
Cannot be used together with `source`.

[§](https://askama.rs#source)source

E.g. `source = "{{ foo }}"`

Directly sets the template source.
This can be useful for test cases or short templates. The generated path
is undefined, which generally makes it impossible to refer to this
template from other templates. If `source` is specified, `ext` must also
be specified (see below). Cannot be used together with `path`.
`ext` (e.g. `ext = "txt"`): lets you specify the content type as a file
extension. This is used to infer an escape mode (see below), and some
web framework integrations use it to determine the content type.
Cannot be used together with `path`.

[§](https://askama.rs#in_doc)`in_doc`

E.g. `in_doc = true`

As an alternative to supplying the code template code in an external file (as `path` argument),
or as a string (as `source` argument), you can also enable the `"code-in-doc"` feature.
With this feature, you can specify the template code directly in the documentation
of the template `struct`.

Instead of `path = "…"` or `source = "…"`, specify `in_doc = true` in the `#[template]`
attribute, and in the struct’s documentation add a `askama` code block:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
/// ```askama
/// <div>{{ lines|linebreaksbr }}</div>
/// ```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(ext = "html", in_doc = true)]
struct Example<'a> {
    lines: &'a str,
}
```
[§](https://askama.rs#print)print

E.g. `print = "code"`

Enable debugging by printing nothing (`none`), the parsed syntax tree (`ast`),
the generated code (`code`) or `all` for both.
The requested data will be printed to stdout at compile time.

[§](https://askama.rs#block)block

E.g. `block = "block_name"`

Renders the block by itself. Expressions outside of the block are not required by the struct, and inheritance is also supported. This can be useful when you need to decompose your template for partial rendering, without needing to extract the partial into a separate template or macro.

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(path = "hello.html", block = "hello")]
struct HelloTemplate<'a> { ... }
```
[§](https://askama.rs#blocks)blocks

E.g. `blocks = ["title", "content"]`

Automatically generates (a number of) sub-templates that act as if they had a
`block = "..."` attribute. You can access the sub-templates with the method
`my_template.as_`, where *block_name*()* block_name* is the
name of the block:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(
    ext = "txt",
    source = "
        {% block title %} ... {% endblock %}
        {% block content %} ... {% endblock %}
    ",
    blocks = ["title", "content"]
)]
struct News<'a> {
    title: &'a str,
    message: &'a str,
}
let news = News {
    title: "Announcing Rust 1.84.1",
    message: "The Rust team has published a new point release of Rust, 1.84.1.",
};
assert_eq!(
    news.as_title().render().unwrap(),
    "<h1>Announcing Rust 1.84.1</h1>"
);
```
[§](https://askama.rs#escape)escape

E.g. `escape = "none"`

Override the template’s extension used for the purpose of determining the escaper for this template. See the section on configuring custom escapers for more information.

[§](https://askama.rs#syntax)syntax

E.g. `syntax = "foo"`

Set the syntax name for a parser defined in the configuration file.
The default syntax, `"default"`,  is the one provided by Askama.

[§](https://askama.rs#askama)askama

E.g. `askama = askama`

If you are using askama in a subproject, a library or a [macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch19-06-macros.html), it might be
necessary to specify the [path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch07-03-paths-for-referring-to-an-item-in-the-module-tree.html) where to find the module `askama`:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[doc(hidden)]
use askama as __askama;
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! new_greeter {
    ($name:ident) => {
        #[derive(Debug, $crate::askama::Template)]
        #[template(
            ext = "txt",
            source = "Hello, world!",
            askama = $crate::__askama
        )]
        struct $name;
    }
}
new_greeter!(HelloWorld);
assert_eq!(HelloWorld.to_string(), Ok("Hello, world."));
```

```
//! [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/askama?logo=rust&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "Crates.io")](https://crates.io/crates/askama)
//! [![GitHub Workflow Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/askama-rs/askama/rust.yml?branch=master&logo=github&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "GitHub Workflow Status")](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/actions/workflows/rust.yml)
//! [![Book](https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/askama?label=book&logo=readthedocs&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "Book")](https://askama.readthedocs.io/)
//! [![docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/askama?logo=docsdotrs&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "docs.rs")](https://docs.rs/askama/)
//!
//! Askama implements a type-safe compiler for Jinja-like templates.
//! It lets you write templates in a Jinja-like syntax,
//! which are linked to a `struct` or an `enum` defining the template context.
//! This is done using a custom derive implementation (implemented
//! in [`askama_derive`](https://crates.io/crates/askama_derive)).
//!
//! For feature highlights and a quick start, please review the
//! [README](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/blob/master/README.md).
//!
//! You can find the documentation about our syntax, features, configuration in our book:
//! [askama.readthedocs.io](https://askama.readthedocs.io/).
//!
//! # Creating Askama templates
//!
//! The main feature of Askama is the [`Template`] derive macro
//! which reads your template code, so your `struct` or `enum` can implement
//! the [`Template`] trait and [`Display`][std::fmt::Display], type-safe and fast:
//!
//! ```rust
//! # use askama::Template;
//! #[derive(Template)]
//! #[template(
//!     ext = "html",
//!     source = "<p>© {{ year }} {{ enterprise|upper }}</p>"
//! )]
//! struct Footer<'a> {
//!     year: u16,
//!     enterprise: &'a str,
//! }
//!
//! assert_eq!(
//!     Footer { year: 2025, enterprise: "<em>Askama</em> developers" }.to_string(),
//!     "<p>© 2025 <EM>ASKAMA</EM> DEVELOPERS</p>",
//! );
//! // In here you see can Askama's auto-escaping. You, the developer,
//! // can easily disable the auto-escaping with the `|safe` filter,
//! // but a malicious user cannot insert e.g. HTML scripts this way.
//! ```
//!
//! An Askama template is a `struct` or `enum` definition which provides the template
//! context combined with a UTF-8 encoded text file (or inline source).
//! Askama can be used to generate any kind of text-based format.
//! The template file's extension may be used to provide content type hints.
//!
//! A template consists of **text contents**, which are passed through as-is,
//! **expressions**, which get replaced with content while being rendered, and
//! **tags**, which control the template's logic.
//! The template syntax is very similar to [Jinja](http://jinja.pocoo.org/),
//! as well as Jinja-derivatives like [Twig](https://twig.symfony.com/) or
//! [Tera](https://github.com/Keats/tera).
#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg, doc_auto_cfg))]

#![deny(unreachable_pub)]
#![deny(missing_docs)]

/// Main `Template` trait; implementations are generally derived
///
/// If you need an object-safe template, use [`DynTemplate`].
///
/// ## Rendering performance
///
/// When rendering a askama template, you should prefer the methods
///
/// * [`.render()`][Template::render] (to render the content into a new string),
/// * [`.render_into()`][Template::render_into] (to render the content into an [`fmt::Write`]
///   object, e.g. [`String`]) or
/// * [`.write_into()`][Template::write_into] (to render the content into an [`io::Write`] object,
///   e.g. [`Vec<u8>`][alloc::vec::Vec])
///
/// over [`.to_string()`][std::string::ToString::to_string] or [`format!()`][alloc::format].
/// While `.to_string()` and `format!()` give you the same result, they generally perform much worse
/// than askama's own methods, because [`fmt::Write`] uses [dynamic methods calls] instead of
/// monomorphised code. On average, expect `.to_string()` to be 100% to 200% slower than
/// `.render()`.
///
/// [dynamic methods calls]: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/keyword.dyn.html>

    }
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer with provided [`Values`].
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn write_into_with_values<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(
        &self,
        writer: &mut W,
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> io::Result<()> {
        struct Wrapped<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html)> {
            writer: W,
            err: Option<[io::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>,
        }
        impl<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html)> [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) for Wrapped<W> {
            fn write_str(&mut self, s: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [fmt::Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/type.Result.html) {
                if let Err(err) = [self](https://askama.rs#163).writer.[write_all](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html#tymethod.write_all)([s](https://askama.rs#163).[as_bytes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/foreigntype.str.html#method.as_bytes)()) {
                    [self](https://askama.rs#163).err = Some([err](https://askama.rs#164));
                    Err([fmt::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/struct.Error.html))
                } else {

                }
            }
        }
        let mut wrapped = [Wrapped](https://askama.rs#157-160) { [writer](https://askama.rs#154), err: None };
        if self.render_into_with_values(&mut wrapped, values).is_ok() {

        } else {
            let err = [wrapped](https://askama.rs#173).err.[take](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.take)();
            Err([err](https://askama.rs#177).[unwrap_or_else](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.unwrap_or_else)(|| [io::Error::new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/error/struct.Error.html#method.new)([io::ErrorKind::Other](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.Other), [fmt::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/struct.Error.html))))
        }
    }
    /// Provides a rough estimate of the expanded length of the rendered template. Larger
    /// values result in higher memory usage but fewer reallocations. Smaller values result in the

    /// [`render_into`], [`write_into`], the [`fmt::Display`] implementation, or the blanket

/// [`dyn`-compatible] wrapper trait around [`Template`] implementers
///
/// This trades reduced performance (mostly due to writing into `dyn Write`) for dyn-compatibility.
///
/// [`dyn`-compatible]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility
pub trait [DynTemplate](https://askama.rs/askama/trait.DynTemplate.html) {
    /// Helper method which allocates a new `String` and renders into it.
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    fn dyn_render(&self) -> Result<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>;
    /// Helper method which allocates a new `String` and renders into it with provided [`Values`].
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    fn dyn_render_with_values(&self, values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37)) -> Result<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` fmt buffer.
    fn dyn_render_into(&self, writer: &mut dyn [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html)) -> Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` fmt buffer with provided [`Values`].
    fn dyn_render_into_with_values(
        &self,
        writer: &mut dyn [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html),
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer.
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn dyn_write_into(&self, writer: &mut dyn [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html)) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer with provided [`Values`].
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn dyn_write_into_with_values(
        &self,
        writer: &mut dyn [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html),
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Provides a conservative estimate of the expanded length of the rendered template.
    fn size_hint(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/primitive.usize.html);
}

/// Implement the trait `$Trait` for a list of reference (wrapper) types to `$T: $Trait + ?Sized`
macro_rules! impl_for_ref {
    (impl $Trait:ident for $T:ident $body:tt) => {
        const _: () = {
            crate::impl_for_ref! {
                impl<$T> $Trait for [
                    &T
                    &mut T
                    core::cell::Ref<'_, T>
                    core::cell::RefMut<'_, T>
                ] $body
            }
        };
        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
        const _: () = {
            crate::impl_for_ref! {
                impl<$T> $Trait for [
                    alloc::boxed::Box<T>
                    alloc::rc::Rc<T>
                    alloc::sync::Arc<T>
                ] $body
            }
        };
        #[cfg(feature = "std")]
        const _: () = {
            crate::impl_for_ref! {
                impl<$T> $Trait for [
                    std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, T>
                    std::sync::RwLockReadGuard<'_, T>
                    std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T>
                ] $body
            }
        };
    };
    (impl<$T:ident> $Trait:ident for [$($ty:ty)*] $body:tt) => {
        $(impl<$T: $Trait + ?Sized> $Trait for $ty $body)*
    }
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc"))]
mod tests {
    use std::fmt;
    use super::*;
    use crate::{DynTemplate, Template};
    #[test]
    fn dyn_template() {
        use alloc::string::ToString;
        struct Test;
        impl Template for Test {
            fn render_into_with_values<W: fmt::Write + ?Sized>(
                &self,
                writer: &mut W,
                _values: &dyn Values,
            ) -> Result<()> {
                Ok(writer.write_str("test")?)
            }
            const SIZE_HINT: usize = 4;
        }
        impl fmt::Display for Test {
            #[inline]
            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                self.render_into(f).map_err(|_| fmt::Error {})
            }
        }
        impl filters::FastWritable for Test {
            #[inline]
            fn write_into<W: fmt::Write + ?Sized>(&self, f: &mut W) -> crate::Result<()> {
                self.render_into(f)
            }
        }
        fn render(t: &dyn DynTemplate) -> String {
            t.dyn_render().unwrap()
        }
        let test = &Test as &dyn DynTemplate;
        assert_eq!(render(test), "test");
        assert_eq!(test.to_string(), "test");
        assert_eq!(alloc::format!("{test}"), "test");
        let mut vec = alloc::vec![];
        test.dyn_write_into(&mut vec).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(vec, alloc::vec![b't', b'e', b's', b't']);
    }
}

Main `Template` trait; implementations are generally derived

If you need an object-safe template, use [ DynTemplate](https://askama.rs/trait.DynTemplate.html).

[§](https://askama.rs#rendering-performance)Rendering performance

When rendering a askama template, you should prefer the methods

- `.render()`
- `.render_into()`- `fmt::Write`- `String`
- `.write_into()`- `io::Write`- `Vec<u8>`

over [ .to_string()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html#tymethod.to_string) or

[. While](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/macro.format.html)

`format!()``.to_string()` and `format!()` give you the same result, they generally perform much worse
than askama’s own methods, because [uses](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html)

`fmt::Write`[dynamic methods calls](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/keyword.dyn.html)instead of monomorphised code. On average, expect

`.to_string()` to be 100% to 200% slower than
`.render()`.## Required Associated Constants[§](https://askama.rs#required-associated-consts)

Provides a rough estimate of the expanded length of the rendered template. Larger
values result in higher memory usage but fewer reallocations. Smaller values result in the
opposite. This value only affects [ render](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html#method.render). It does not take effect when calling

[,](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html#method.render_into)

`render_into`[, the](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html#method.write_into)

`write_into`[implementation, or the blanket](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html)

# Template in askama - Rust

Source: https://askama.rs/en/v0.13.1/doc/askama/derive.Template.html

```
#[derive(Template)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[template]
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`derive`## Expand description

The `Template` derive macro and its `template()` attribute.

Askama works by generating one or more trait implementations for any
`struct` type decorated with the `#[derive(Template)]` attribute. The
code generation process takes some options that can be specified through
the `template()` attribute.

[§](https://askama.rs#attributes)Attributes

The following sub-attributes are currently recognized:

[§](https://askama.rs#path)path

E.g. `path = "foo.html"`

Sets the path to the template file.
The path is interpreted as relative to the configured template directories
(by default, this is a `templates` directory next to your `Cargo.toml`).
The file name extension is used to infer an escape mode (see below). In
web framework integrations, the path’s extension may also be used to
infer the content type of the resulting response.
Cannot be used together with `source`.

[§](https://askama.rs#source)source

E.g. `source = "{{ foo }}"`

Directly sets the template source.
This can be useful for test cases or short templates. The generated path
is undefined, which generally makes it impossible to refer to this
template from other templates. If `source` is specified, `ext` must also
be specified (see below). Cannot be used together with `path`.
`ext` (e.g. `ext = "txt"`): lets you specify the content type as a file
extension. This is used to infer an escape mode (see below), and some
web framework integrations use it to determine the content type.
Cannot be used together with `path`.

[§](https://askama.rs#in_doc)`in_doc`

E.g. `in_doc = true`

As an alternative to supplying the code template code in an external file (as `path` argument),
or as a string (as `source` argument), you can also enable the `"code-in-doc"` feature.
With this feature, you can specify the template code directly in the documentation
of the template `struct`.

Instead of `path = "…"` or `source = "…"`, specify `in_doc = true` in the `#[template]`
attribute, and in the struct’s documentation add a `askama` code block:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
/// ```askama
/// <div>{{ lines|linebreaksbr }}</div>
/// ```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(ext = "html", in_doc = true)]
struct Example<'a> {
    lines: &'a str,
}
```
[§](https://askama.rs#print)print

E.g. `print = "code"`

Enable debugging by printing nothing (`none`), the parsed syntax tree (`ast`),
the generated code (`code`) or `all` for both.
The requested data will be printed to stdout at compile time.

[§](https://askama.rs#block)block

E.g. `block = "block_name"`

Renders the block by itself. Expressions outside of the block are not required by the struct, and inheritance is also supported. This can be useful when you need to decompose your template for partial rendering, without needing to extract the partial into a separate template or macro.

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(path = "hello.html", block = "hello")]
struct HelloTemplate<'a> { ... }
```
[§](https://askama.rs#blocks)blocks

E.g. `blocks = ["title", "content"]`

Automatically generates (a number of) sub-templates that act as if they had a
`block = "..."` attribute. You can access the sub-templates with the method
`my_template.as_`, where *block_name*()* block_name* is the
name of the block:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(
    ext = "txt",
    source = "
        {% block title %} ... {% endblock %}
        {% block content %} ... {% endblock %}
    ",
    blocks = ["title", "content"]
)]
struct News<'a> {
    title: &'a str,
    message: &'a str,
}
let news = News {
    title: "Announcing Rust 1.84.1",
    message: "The Rust team has published a new point release of Rust, 1.84.1.",
};
assert_eq!(
    news.as_title().render().unwrap(),
    "<h1>Announcing Rust 1.84.1</h1>"
);
```
[§](https://askama.rs#escape)escape

E.g. `escape = "none"`

Override the template’s extension used for the purpose of determining the escaper for this template. See the section on configuring custom escapers for more information.

[§](https://askama.rs#syntax)syntax

E.g. `syntax = "foo"`

Set the syntax name for a parser defined in the configuration file.
The default syntax, `"default"`,  is the one provided by Askama.

[§](https://askama.rs#askama)askama

E.g. `askama = askama`

If you are using askama in a subproject, a library or a [macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch19-06-macros.html), it might be
necessary to specify the [path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch07-03-paths-for-referring-to-an-item-in-the-module-tree.html) where to find the module `askama`:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[doc(hidden)]
use askama as __askama;
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! new_greeter {
    ($name:ident) => {
        #[derive(Debug, $crate::askama::Template)]
        #[template(
            ext = "txt",
            source = "Hello, world!",
            askama = $crate::__askama
        )]
        struct $name;
    }
}
new_greeter!(HelloWorld);
assert_eq!(HelloWorld.to_string(), Ok("Hello, world."));
```

```
//! [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/askama?logo=rust&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "Crates.io")](https://crates.io/crates/askama)
//! [![GitHub Workflow Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/askama-rs/askama/rust.yml?branch=master&logo=github&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "GitHub Workflow Status")](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/actions/workflows/rust.yml)
//! [![Book](https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/askama?label=book&logo=readthedocs&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "Book")](https://askama.readthedocs.io/)
//! [![docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/askama?logo=docsdotrs&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "docs.rs")](https://docs.rs/askama/)
//!
//! Askama implements a type-safe compiler for Jinja-like templates.
//! It lets you write templates in a Jinja-like syntax,
//! which are linked to a `struct` or an `enum` defining the template context.
//! This is done using a custom derive implementation (implemented
//! in [`askama_derive`](https://crates.io/crates/askama_derive)).
//!
//! For feature highlights and a quick start, please review the
//! [README](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/blob/master/README.md).
//!
//! You can find the documentation about our syntax, features, configuration in our book:
//! [askama.readthedocs.io](https://askama.readthedocs.io/).
//!
//! # Creating Askama templates
//!
//! The main feature of Askama is the [`Template`] derive macro
//! which reads your template code, so your `struct` or `enum` can implement
//! the [`Template`] trait and [`Display`][std::fmt::Display], type-safe and fast:
//!
//! ```rust
//! # use askama::Template;
//! #[derive(Template)]
//! #[template(
//!     ext = "html",
//!     source = "<p>© {{ year }} {{ enterprise|upper }}</p>"
//! )]
//! struct Footer<'a> {
//!     year: u16,
//!     enterprise: &'a str,
//! }
//!
//! assert_eq!(
//!     Footer { year: 2025, enterprise: "<em>Askama</em> developers" }.to_string(),
//!     "<p>© 2025 <EM>ASKAMA</EM> DEVELOPERS</p>",
//! );
//! // In here you see can Askama's auto-escaping. You, the developer,
//! // can easily disable the auto-escaping with the `|safe` filter,
//! // but a malicious user cannot insert e.g. HTML scripts this way.
//! ```
//!
//! An Askama template is a `struct` or `enum` definition which provides the template
//! context combined with a UTF-8 encoded text file (or inline source).
//! Askama can be used to generate any kind of text-based format.
//! The template file's extension may be used to provide content type hints.
//!
//! A template consists of **text contents**, which are passed through as-is,
//! **expressions**, which get replaced with content while being rendered, and
//! **tags**, which control the template's logic.
//! The template syntax is very similar to [Jinja](http://jinja.pocoo.org/),
//! as well as Jinja-derivatives like [Twig](https://twig.symfony.com/) or
//! [Tera](https://github.com/Keats/tera).
#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg, doc_auto_cfg))]
#![deny(elided_lifetimes_in_paths)]
#![deny(unreachable_pub)]
#![deny(missing_docs)]
#![no_std]
#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
extern crate alloc;
#[cfg(feature = "std")]
extern crate std;

/// Main `Template` trait; implementations are generally derived
///
/// If you need an object-safe template, use [`DynTemplate`].
///
/// ## Rendering performance
///
/// When rendering a askama template, you should prefer the methods
///
/// * [`.render()`][Template::render] (to render the content into a new string),
/// * [`.render_into()`][Template::render_into] (to render the content into an [`fmt::Write`]
///   object, e.g. [`String`]) or
/// * [`.write_into()`][Template::write_into] (to render the content into an [`io::Write`] object,
///   e.g. [`Vec<u8>`][alloc::vec::Vec])
///
/// over [`.to_string()`][std::string::ToString::to_string] or [`format!()`][alloc::format].
/// While `.to_string()` and `format!()` give you the same result, they generally perform much worse
/// than askama's own methods, because [`fmt::Write`] uses [dynamic methods calls] instead of
/// monomorphised code. On average, expect `.to_string()` to be 100% to 200% slower than
/// `.render()`.
///
/// [dynamic methods calls]: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/keyword.dyn.html>
pub trait [Template](https://askama.rs/askama/trait.Template.html): [fmt::Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) + [filters::FastWritable](https://askama.rs/filters/escape.rs.html#504-507) {
    /// Helper method which allocates a new `String` and renders into it.
    #[inline]
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    fn render(&self) -> Result<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html)> {
        [self](https://askama.rs#116).[render_with_values](https://askama.rs#123-128)([NO_VALUES](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#7))
    }
    /// Helper method which allocates a new `String` and renders into it with provided [`Values`].
    #[inline]
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    fn render_with_values(&self, values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37)) -> Result<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html)> {
        let mut buf = [String::new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.new)();
        let _ = [buf](https://askama.rs#124).[try_reserve](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.try_reserve)(Self::SIZE_HINT);
        [self](https://askama.rs#123).[render_into_with_values](https://askama.rs#137-141)(&mut [buf](https://askama.rs#124), [values](https://askama.rs#123))?;
        Ok([buf](https://askama.rs#124))
    }
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` fmt buffer.
    #[inline]
    fn render_into<W: [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(&self, writer: &mut W) -> Result<()> {
        [self](https://askama.rs#132).[render_into_with_values](https://askama.rs#137-141)([writer](https://askama.rs#132), [NO_VALUES](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#7))
    }
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` fmt buffer with provided [`Values`].
    fn render_into_with_values<W: [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(
        &self,
        writer: &mut W,
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer.
    #[inline]
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn write_into<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(&self, writer: &mut W) -> io::Result<()> {
        [self](https://askama.rs#146).[write_into_with_values](https://askama.rs#152-180)([writer](https://askama.rs#146), [NO_VALUES](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#7))
    }
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer with provided [`Values`].
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn write_into_with_values<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(
        &self,
        writer: &mut W,
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> io::Result<()> {
        struct Wrapped<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html)> {
            writer: W,
            err: Option<[io::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>,
        }
        impl<W: [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html)> [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) for Wrapped<W> {
            fn write_str(&mut self, s: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [fmt::Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/type.Result.html) {
                if let Err(err) = [self](https://askama.rs#163).writer.[write_all](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html#tymethod.write_all)([s](https://askama.rs#163).[as_bytes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/foreigntype.str.html#method.as_bytes)()) {
                    [self](https://askama.rs#163).err = Some([err](https://askama.rs#164));
                    Err([fmt::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/struct.Error.html))
                } else {
                    Ok(())
                }
            }
        }
        let mut wrapped = [Wrapped](https://askama.rs#157-160) { [writer](https://askama.rs#154), err: None };
        if self.render_into_with_values(&mut wrapped, values).is_ok() {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            let err = [wrapped](https://askama.rs#173).err.[take](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.take)();
            Err([err](https://askama.rs#177).[unwrap_or_else](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.unwrap_or_else)(|| [io::Error::new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/error/struct.Error.html#method.new)([io::ErrorKind::Other](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.Other), [fmt::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/struct.Error.html))))
        }
    }

    /// opposite. This value only affects [`render`]. It does not take effect when calling
    /// [`render_into`], [`write_into`], the [`fmt::Display`] implementation, or the blanket
    /// [`ToString::to_string`] implementation.

    /// [`render`]: Template::render

    /// [`write_into`]: Template::write_into

/// [`dyn`-compatible] wrapper trait around [`Template`] implementers
///
/// This trades reduced performance (mostly due to writing into `dyn Write`) for dyn-compatibility.
///
/// [`dyn`-compatible]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility
pub trait [DynTemplate](https://askama.rs/askama/trait.DynTemplate.html) {
    /// Helper method which allocates a new `String` and renders into it.
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    fn dyn_render(&self) -> Result<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>;
    /// Helper method which allocates a new `String` and renders into it with provided [`Values`].
    #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
    fn dyn_render_with_values(&self, values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37)) -> Result<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` fmt buffer.
    fn dyn_render_into(&self, writer: &mut dyn [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html)) -> Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` fmt buffer with provided [`Values`].
    fn dyn_render_into_with_values(
        &self,
        writer: &mut dyn [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html),
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer.
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn dyn_write_into(&self, writer: &mut dyn [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html)) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Renders the template to the given `writer` io buffer with provided [`Values`].
    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
    fn dyn_write_into_with_values(
        &self,
        writer: &mut dyn [io::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/io/trait.Write.html),
        values: &dyn [Values](https://askama.rs/values.rs.html#34-37),
    ) -> io::Result<()>;
    /// Provides a conservative estimate of the expanded length of the rendered template.
    fn size_hint(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.82.0/std/primitive.usize.html);
}

/// Implement the trait `$Trait` for a list of reference (wrapper) types to `$T: $Trait + ?Sized`
macro_rules! impl_for_ref {
    (impl $Trait:ident for $T:ident $body:tt) => {
        const _: () = {
            crate::impl_for_ref! {
                impl<$T> $Trait for [
                    &T
                    &mut T
                    core::cell::Ref<'_, T>
                    core::cell::RefMut<'_, T>
                ] $body
            }
        };
        #[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
        const _: () = {
            crate::impl_for_ref! {
                impl<$T> $Trait for [
                    alloc::boxed::Box<T>
                    alloc::rc::Rc<T>
                    alloc::sync::Arc<T>
                ] $body
            }
        };
        #[cfg(feature = "std")]
        const _: () = {
            crate::impl_for_ref! {
                impl<$T> $Trait for [
                    std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, T>
                    std::sync::RwLockReadGuard<'_, T>
                    std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T>
                ] $body
            }
        };
    };
    (impl<$T:ident> $Trait:ident for [$($ty:ty)*] $body:tt) => {
        $(impl<$T: $Trait + ?Sized> $Trait for $ty $body)*
    }
}
pub(crate) use [impl_for_ref](https://askama.rs#335-371);
#[cfg(all(test, feature = "alloc"))]
mod tests {
    use std::fmt;
    use super::*;
    use crate::{DynTemplate, Template};
    #[test]
    fn dyn_template() {
        use alloc::string::ToString;
        struct Test;
        impl Template for Test {
            fn render_into_with_values<W: fmt::Write + ?Sized>(
                &self,
                writer: &mut W,
                _values: &dyn Values,
            ) -> Result<()> {
                Ok(writer.write_str("test")?)
            }
            const SIZE_HINT: usize = 4;
        }
        impl fmt::Display for Test {
            #[inline]
            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                self.render_into(f).map_err(|_| fmt::Error {})
            }
        }
        impl filters::FastWritable for Test {
            #[inline]
            fn write_into<W: fmt::Write + ?Sized>(&self, f: &mut W) -> crate::Result<()> {
                self.render_into(f)
            }
        }
        fn render(t: &dyn DynTemplate) -> String {
            t.dyn_render().unwrap()
        }
        let test = &Test as &dyn DynTemplate;
        assert_eq!(render(test), "test");
        assert_eq!(test.to_string(), "test");
        assert_eq!(alloc::format!("{test}"), "test");
        let mut vec = alloc::vec![];
        test.dyn_write_into(&mut vec).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(vec, alloc::vec![b't', b'e', b's', b't']);
    }
}

`derive`## Expand description

The `Template` derive macro and its `template()` attribute.

Askama works by generating one or more trait implementations for any
`struct` type decorated with the `#[derive(Template)]` attribute. The
code generation process takes some options that can be specified through
the `template()` attribute.

[§](https://askama.rs#attributes)Attributes

The following sub-attributes are currently recognized:

[§](https://askama.rs#path)path

E.g. `path = "foo.html"`

Sets the path to the template file.
The path is interpreted as relative to the configured template directories
(by default, this is a `templates` directory next to your `Cargo.toml`).
The file name extension is used to infer an escape mode (see below). In
web framework integrations, the path’s extension may also be used to
infer the content type of the resulting response.
Cannot be used together with `source`.

[§](https://askama.rs#source)source

E.g. `source = "{{ foo }}"`

Directly sets the template source.
This can be useful for test cases or short templates. The generated path
is undefined, which generally makes it impossible to refer to this
template from other templates. If `source` is specified, `ext` must also
be specified (see below). Cannot be used together with `path`.
`ext` (e.g. `ext = "txt"`): lets you specify the content type as a file
extension. This is used to infer an escape mode (see below), and some
web framework integrations use it to determine the content type.
Cannot be used together with `path`.

[§](https://askama.rs#in_doc)`in_doc`

E.g. `in_doc = true`

As an alternative to supplying the code template code in an external file (as `path` argument),
or as a string (as `source` argument), you can also enable the `"code-in-doc"` feature.
With this feature, you can specify the template code directly in the documentation
of the template `struct`.

Instead of `path = "…"` or `source = "…"`, specify `in_doc = true` in the `#[template]`
attribute, and in the struct’s documentation add a `askama` code block:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
/// ```askama
/// <div>{{ lines|linebreaksbr }}</div>
/// ```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(ext = "html", in_doc = true)]
struct Example<'a> {
    lines: &'a str,
}
```
[§](https://askama.rs#print)print

E.g. `print = "code"`

Enable debugging by printing nothing (`none`), the parsed syntax tree (`ast`),
the generated code (`code`) or `all` for both.
The requested data will be printed to stdout at compile time.

[§](https://askama.rs#block)block

E.g. `block = "block_name"`

Renders the block by itself. Expressions outside of the block are not required by the struct, and inheritance is also supported. This can be useful when you need to decompose your template for partial rendering, without needing to extract the partial into a separate template or macro.

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(path = "hello.html", block = "hello")]
struct HelloTemplate<'a> { ... }
```
[§](https://askama.rs#blocks)blocks

E.g. `blocks = ["title", "content"]`

Automatically generates (a number of) sub-templates that act as if they had a
`block = "..."` attribute. You can access the sub-templates with the method
`my_template.as_`, where *block_name*()* block_name* is the
name of the block:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(
    ext = "txt",
    source = "
        {% block title %} ... {% endblock %}
        {% block content %} ... {% endblock %}
    ",
    blocks = ["title", "content"]
)]
struct News<'a> {
    title: &'a str,
    message: &'a str,
}
let news = News {
    title: "Announcing Rust 1.84.1",
    message: "The Rust team has published a new point release of Rust, 1.84.1.",
};
assert_eq!(
    news.as_title().render().unwrap(),
    "<h1>Announcing Rust 1.84.1</h1>"
);
```
[§](https://askama.rs#escape)escape

E.g. `escape = "none"`

Override the template’s extension used for the purpose of determining the escaper for this template. See the section on configuring custom escapers for more information.

[§](https://askama.rs#syntax)syntax

E.g. `syntax = "foo"`

Set the syntax name for a parser defined in the configuration file.
The default syntax, `"default"`,  is the one provided by Askama.

[§](https://askama.rs#askama)askama

E.g. `askama = askama`

If you are using askama in a subproject, a library or a [macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch19-06-macros.html), it might be
necessary to specify the [path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch07-03-paths-for-referring-to-an-item-in-the-module-tree.html) where to find the module `askama`:

[ⓘ](https://askama.rs)

```
#[doc(hidden)]
use askama as __askama;
#[macro_export]
macro_rules! new_greeter {
    ($name:ident) => {
        #[derive(Debug, $crate::askama::Template)]
        #[template(
            ext = "txt",
            source = "Hello, world!",
            askama = $crate::__askama
        )]
        struct $name;
    }
}
new_greeter!(HelloWorld);
assert_eq!(HelloWorld.to_string(), Ok("Hello, world."));
```

---

# askama - Rust

Source: https://askama.rs/en/latest/doc/askama/index.html

## Expand description

Askama implements a type-safe compiler for Jinja-like templates.
It lets you write templates in a Jinja-like syntax,
which are linked to a `struct` or an `enum` defining the template context.
This is done using a custom derive implementation (implemented
in [ askama_macros](https://crates.io/crates/askama_macros)).

For feature highlights and a quick start, please review the
[README](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/blob/main/README.md).

You can find the documentation about our syntax, features, configuration in our book:
[askama.rs](https://askama.rs/).

[§](https://askama.rs#creating-askama-templates)Creating Askama templates

The main feature of Askama is the [ Template](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html) derive macro
which reads your template code, so your

`struct` or `enum` can implement
the [trait and](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html)

`Template`[, type-safe and fast:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html)

`Display````
#[derive(Template)]
#[template(
    ext = "html",
    source = "<p>© {{ year }} {{ enterprise|upper }}</p>"
)]
struct Footer<'a> {
    year: u16,
    enterprise: &'a str,
}
assert_eq!(
    Footer { year: 2025, enterprise: "<em>Askama</em> developers" }.to_string(),
    "<p>© 2025 <EM>ASKAMA</EM> DEVELOPERS</p>",
);
// In here you see can Askama's auto-escaping. You, the developer,
// can easily disable the auto-escaping with the `|safe` filter,
// but a malicious user cannot insert e.g. HTML scripts this way.
```
An Askama template is a `struct` or `enum` definition which provides the template
context combined with a UTF-8 encoded text file (or inline source).
Askama can be used to generate any kind of text-based format.
The template file’s extension may be used to provide content type hints.

A template consists of **text contents**, which are passed through as-is,
**expressions**, which get replaced with content while being rendered, and
**tags**, which control the template’s logic.
The template syntax is very similar to [Jinja](http://jinja.pocoo.org/),
as well as Jinja-derivatives like [Twig](https://twig.symfony.com/) or
[Tera](https://github.com/Keats/tera).

- [Primitive](https://askama.rs/trait.PrimitiveType.html)- Type

- A runtime value store for `Template::render_with_values()`

}## Expand description

Main `Template` trait; implementations are generally derived

If you need an object-safe template, use [ DynTemplate](https://askama.rs/trait.DynTemplate.html).

[§](https://askama.rs#rendering-performance)Rendering performance

When rendering a askama template, you should prefer the methods

- `.render()`
- `.render_into()`- `fmt::Write`- `String`
- `.write_into()`- `io::Write`- `Vec<u8>`

over [ .to_string()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html#tymethod.to_string) or

[. While](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/macro.format.html)

`format!()``.to_string()` and `format!()` give you the same result, they generally perform much worse
than askama’s own methods, because [uses](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html)

`fmt::Write`[dynamic methods calls](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/keyword.dyn.html)instead of monomorphised code. On average, expect

`.to_string()` to be 100% to 200% slower than
`.render()`.## Required Associated Constants[§](https://askama.rs#required-associated-consts)

Provides a rough estimate of the expanded length of the rendered template. Larger
values result in higher memory usage but fewer reallocations. Smaller values result in the
opposite. This value only affects [ render](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html#method.render). It does not take effect when calling

[,](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html#method.render_into)

`render_into`[, the](https://askama.rs/trait.Template.html#method.write_into)

`write_into`[implementation, or the blanket](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html)

`fmt::Display`[implementation.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html#tymethod.to_string)

`ToString::to_string`## Required Methods[§](https://askama.rs#required-methods)

# askama/lib.rs

[1](https://askama.rs#1)//! [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/askama?logo=rust&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "Crates.io")](https://crates.io/crates/askama)
[2](https://askama.rs#2)//! [![GitHub Workflow Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/askama-rs/askama/rust.yml?branch=main&logo=github&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "GitHub Workflow Status")](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/actions/workflows/rust.yml)
[3](https://askama.rs#3)//! [![Book](https://img.shields.io/readthedocs/askama?label=book&logo=readthedocs&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "Book")](https://askama.rs/)
[4](https://askama.rs#4)//! [![docs.rs](https://img.shields.io/docsrs/askama?logo=docsdotrs&style=flat-square&logoColor=white "docs.rs")](https://docs.rs/askama/)
[5](https://askama.rs#5)//!
[6](https://askama.rs#6)//! Askama implements a type-safe compiler for Jinja-like templates.
[7](https://askama.rs#7)//! It lets you write templates in a Jinja-like syntax,
[8](https://askama.rs#8)//! which are linked to a `struct` or an `enum` defining the template context.
[9](https://askama.rs#9)//! This is done using a custom derive implementation (implemented
[10](https://askama.rs#10)//! in [`askama_macros`](https://crates.io/crates/askama_macros)).
[11](https://askama.rs#11)//!
[12](https://askama.rs#12)//! For feature highlights and a quick start, please review the
[13](https://askama.rs#13)//! [README](https://github.com/askama-rs/askama/blob/main/README.md).
[14](https://askama.rs#14)//!
[15](https://askama.rs#15)//! You can find the documentation about our syntax, features, configuration in our book:
[16](https://askama.rs#16)//! [askama.rs](https://askama.rs/).
[17](https://askama.rs#17)//!
[18](https://askama.rs#18)//! # Creating Askama templates
[19](https://askama.rs#19)//!
[20](https://askama.rs#20)//! The main feature of Askama is the [`Template`] derive macro
[21](https://askama.rs#21)//! which reads your template code, so your `struct` or `enum` can implement
[22](https://askama.rs#22)//! the [`Template`] trait and [`Display`][std::fmt::Display], type-safe and fast:
[23](https://askama.rs#23)//!
[24](https://askama.rs#24)//! ```rust
[25](https://askama.rs#25)//! # use askama::Template;
[26](https://askama.rs#26)//! #[derive(Template)]
[27](https://askama.rs#27)//! #[template(
[28](https://askama.rs#28)//!     ext = "html",
[29](https://askama.rs#29)//!     source = "<p>© {{ year }} {{ enterprise|upper }}</p>"
[30](https://askama.rs#30)//! )]
[31](https://askama.rs#31)//! struct Footer<'a> {
[32](https://askama.rs#32)//!     year: u16,
[33](https://askama.rs#33)//!     enterprise: &'a str,
[34](https://askama.rs#34)//! }
[35](https://askama.rs#35)//!
[36](https://askama.rs#36)//! assert_eq!(
[37](https://askama.rs#37)//!     Footer { year: 2025, enterprise: "<em>Askama</em> developers" }.to_string(),
[38](https://askama.rs#38)//!     "<p>© 2025 <EM>ASKAMA</EM> DEVELOPERS</p>",
[39](https://askama.rs#39)//! );
[40](https://askama.rs#40)//! // In here you see can Askama's auto-escaping. You, the developer,
[41](https://askama.rs#41)//! // can easily disable the auto-escaping with the `|safe` filter,
[42](https://askama.rs#42)//! // but a malicious user cannot insert e.g. HTML scripts this way.
[43](https://askama.rs#43)//! ```
[44](https://askama.rs#44)//!
[45](https://askama.rs#45)//! An Askama template is a `struct` or `enum` definition which provides the template
[46](https://askama.rs#46)//! context combined with a UTF-8 encoded text file (or inline source).
[47](https://askama.rs#47)//! Askama can be used to generate any kind of text-based format.
[48](https://askama.rs#48)//! The template file's extension may be used to provide content type hints.
[49](https://askama.rs#49)//!
[50](https://askama.rs#50)//! A template consists of **text contents**, which are passed through as-is,
[51](https://askama.rs#51)//! **expressions**, which get replaced with content while being rendered, and
[52](https://askama.rs#52)//! **tags**, which control the template's logic.
[53](https://askama.rs#53)//! The template syntax is very similar to [Jinja](http://jinja.pocoo.org/),
[54](https://askama.rs#54)//! as well as Jinja-derivatives like [Twig](https://twig.symfony.com/) or
[55](https://askama.rs#55)//! [Tera](https://github.com/Keats/tera).
[56](https://askama.rs#56)

[92](https://askama.rs#92)/// Main `Template` trait; implementations are generally derived

[94](https://askama.rs#94)/// If you need an object-safe template, use [`DynTemplate`].
[95](https://askama.rs#95)///
[96](https://askama.rs#96)/// ## Rendering performance
[97](https://askama.rs#97)///
[98](https://askama.rs#98)/// When rendering a askama template, you should prefer the methods
[99](https://askama.rs#99)///
[100](https://askama.rs#100)/// * [`.render()`][Template::render] (to render the content into a new string),
[101](https://askama.rs#101)/// * [`.render_into()`][Template::render_into] (to render the content into an [`fmt::Write`]
[102](https://askama.rs#102)///   object, e.g. [`String`]) or
[103](https://askama.rs#103)/// * [`.write_into()`][Template::write_into] (to render the content into an [`io::Write`] object,
[104](https://askama.rs#104)///   e.g. [`Vec<u8>`][alloc::vec::Vec])
[105](https://askama.rs#105)///
[106](https://askama.rs#106)/// over [`.to_string()`][std::string::ToString::to_string] or [`format!()`][alloc::format].
[107](https://askama.rs#107)/// While `.to_string()` and `format!()` give you the same result, they generally perform much worse
[108](https://askama.rs#108)/// than askama's own methods, because [`fmt::Write`] uses [dynamic methods calls] instead of
[109](https://askama.rs#109)/// monomorphised code. On average, expect `.to_string()` to be 100% to 200% slower than
[110](https://askama.rs#110)/// `.render()`.
[111](https://askama.rs#111)///
[112](https://askama.rs#112)/// [dynamic methods calls]: <https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/keyword.dyn.html>

}

Contains the success value

The contained value

An error that prevented

`as_filtered()` to succeed,
e.g. a poisoned state or an unacquirable lock.

Return the contained value, if a value was contained, and it’s not the default value.

[148](https://askama.rs#148)/// Result of the filter [`join()`].
[149](https://askama.rs#149)///
[150](https://askama.rs#150)/// ## Note
[151](https://askama.rs#151)///
[152](https://askama.rs#152)/// This struct implements [`fmt::Display`], but only produces a string once.
[153](https://askama.rs#153)/// Any subsequent call to `.to_string()` will result in an empty string, because the iterator is
[154](https://askama.rs#154)/// already consumed.
[155](https://askama.rs#155)// The filter contains a [`Cell`], so we can modify iterator inside a method that takes `self` by
[156](https://askama.rs#156)// reference: [`fmt::Display::fmt()`] normally has the contract that it will produce the same result
[157](https://askama.rs#157)// in multiple invocations for the same object. We break this contract, because have to consume the
[158](https://askama.rs#158)// iterator, unless we want to enforce `I: Clone`, nor do we want to "memorize" the result of the
[159](https://askama.rs#159)// joined data.
[160](https://askama.rs#160)pub struct JoinFilter<I, S>([Cell](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/cell/struct.Cell.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(I, S)>>);
[161](https://askama.rs#161)
[162](https://askama.rs#162)impl<I, S> [fmt::Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) for [JoinFilter](https://askama.rs#160)<I, S>
[163](https://askama.rs#163)where
[164](https://askama.rs#164)    I: [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html),
[165](https://askama.rs#165)    I::Item: [fmt::Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html),
[166](https://askama.rs#166)    S: [fmt::Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html),
[167](https://askama.rs#167){
[168](https://askama.rs#168)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut [fmt::Formatter](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/struct.Formatter.html)<'_>) -> [fmt::Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/type.Result.html) {
[169](https://askama.rs#169)        let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)((iter, separator)) = [self](https://askama.rs#168).0.[take](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/cell/struct.Cell.html#method.take)() else {
[170](https://askama.rs#170)            return [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(());
[171](https://askama.rs#171)        };
[172](https://askama.rs#172)        for (idx, token) in iter.into_iter().enumerate() {
[173](https://askama.rs#173)            match idx {
[174](https://askama.rs#174)                0 => f.write_fmt(format_args!("{token}"))?,
[175](https://askama.rs#175)                _ => f.write_fmt(format_args!("{separator}{token}"))?,
[176](https://askama.rs#176)            }
[177](https://askama.rs#177)        }
[178](https://askama.rs#178)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(())
[179](https://askama.rs#179)    }

[330](https://askama.rs#330)#[inline]
[331](https://askama.rs#331)pub fn [pluralize](https://askama.rs/askama/filters/fn.pluralize.html)<C, S, P>(count: C, singular: S, plural: P) -> [Result](https://askama.rs/error.rs.html#11)<[Either](https://askama.rs#428-433)<S, P>, C::Error>

[585](https://askama.rs#585)impl<'a> [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) for [WordCountWriter](https://askama.rs#583)<'a> {
[586](https://askama.rs#586)    fn write_str(&mut self, s: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [fmt::Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/type.Result.html) {
[587](https://askama.rs#587)        if s.is_empty() {
[588](https://askama.rs#588)            // If the input is empty, nothing to be done.
[589](https://askama.rs#589)            return [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(());
[590](https://askama.rs#590)        } else if s.trim().is_empty() {
[591](https://askama.rs#591)            // If the input only contains whitespace characters, we set `ends_with_whitespace` to
[592](https://askama.rs#592)            // `true`. It is to handle this case: `["a", " ", "b"]`. In total we should have two
[593](https://askama.rs#593)            // words count.
[594](https://askama.rs#594)            [self](https://askama.rs#586).0.ends_with_whitespace = true;
[595](https://askama.rs#595)            return [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(());
[596](https://askama.rs#596)        }
[597](https://askama.rs#597)        [self](https://askama.rs#586).0.count += [s](https://askama.rs#586).[split_whitespace](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/foreigntype.str.html#method.split_whitespace)().[count](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#tymethod.count)();
[598](https://askama.rs#598)        if !self.0.ends_with_whitespace && !s.starts_with(char::is_whitespace) {
[599](https://askama.rs#599)            // This covers this case: `["a", "b c"]`. Here, we have two words ("ab" and "c") so we
[600](https://askama.rs#600)            // need to subtract one from the count on "b c" because it returns 2 whereas "a" word is
[601](https://askama.rs#601)            // not "finished".
[602](https://askama.rs#602)            [self](https://askama.rs#586).0.count -= 1;
[603](https://askama.rs#603)        }
[604](https://askama.rs#604)        // And again, if the string ends with a whitespace character, we change the value of
[605](https://askama.rs#605)        // `ends_with_whitespace`.
[606](https://askama.rs#606)        [self](https://askama.rs#586).0.ends_with_whitespace = [s](https://askama.rs#586).[ends_with](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/foreigntype.str.html#method.ends_with)(char::is_whitespace);
[607](https://askama.rs#607)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(())
[608](https://askama.rs#608)    }

[716](https://askama.rs#716)struct NewlineCountingFormatter<'a, W: ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> {
[717](https://askama.rs#717)    dest: &'a mut W,
[718](https://askama.rs#718)    counter: [isize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.isize.html),
[719](https://askama.rs#719)    one: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html),
[720](https://askama.rs#720)}
[721](https://askama.rs#721)
[722](https://askama.rs#722)impl<W: [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> [fmt::Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) for [NewlineCountingFormatter](https://askama.rs#716-720)<'_, W> {
[723](https://askama.rs#723)    fn write_str(&mut self, s: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [fmt::Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/type.Result.html) {
[724](https://askama.rs#724)        if s.is_empty() {
[725](https://askama.rs#725)            return [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(());
[726](https://askama.rs#726)        }
[727](https://askama.rs#727)        for (has_eol, line) in split_lines(s) {
[728](https://askama.rs#728)            if !line.is_empty() {
[729](https://askama.rs#729)                match replace(&mut self.counter, if has_eol { 1 } else { 0 }) {
[730](https://askama.rs#730)                    ..=0 => {}
[731](https://askama.rs#731)                    1 => self.dest.write_str(self.one)?,
[732](https://askama.rs#732)                    2.. => self.dest.write_str("</p><p>")?,
[733](https://askama.rs#733)                }
[734](https://askama.rs#734)                self.dest.write_str(line)?;
[735](https://askama.rs#735)            } else if has_eol && self.counter >= 0 {
[736](https://askama.rs#736)                self.counter += 1;
[737](https://askama.rs#737)            }
[738](https://askama.rs#738)        }
[739](https://askama.rs#739)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(())
[740](https://askama.rs#740)    }

[807](https://askama.rs#807)/// Splits the input at `/\r?\n/g``; returns whether a newline suffix was stripped and the
[808](https://askama.rs#808)/// (maybe stripped) line.

[218](https://askama.rs#218)/// Types that implement this marker trait don't need to be HTML escaped
[219](https://askama.rs#219)///
[220](https://askama.rs#220)/// Please note that this trait is only meant as speed-up helper. In some odd circumcises askama
[221](https://askama.rs#221)/// might still decide to HTML escape the input, so if this must not happen, then you need to use
[222](https://askama.rs#222)/// the [`|safe`](super::safe) filter to prevent the auto escaping.
[223](https://askama.rs#223)///
[224](https://askama.rs#224)/// If you are unsure if your type generates HTML safe output in all cases, then DON'T mark it.
[225](https://askama.rs#225)/// Better safe than sorry!

[238](https://askama.rs#238)
[239](https://askama.rs#239)/// Mark the output of a filter as "maybe safe"
[240](https://askama.rs#240)///
[241](https://askama.rs#241)/// This enum can be used as a transparent return type of custom filters that want to mark
[242](https://askama.rs#242)/// their output as "safe" depending on some circumstances, i.e. that their output maybe does not
[243](https://askama.rs#243)/// need to be escaped.
[244](https://askama.rs#244)///
[245](https://askama.rs#245)/// If the filter is not used as the last element in the filter chain, then any assumption is void.
[246](https://askama.rs#246)/// Let the next filter decide if the output is safe or not.
[247](https://askama.rs#247)///
[248](https://askama.rs#248)/// ## Example
[249](https://askama.rs#249)///
[250](https://askama.rs#250)/// ```rust
[251](https://askama.rs#251)/// mod filters {
[252](https://askama.rs#252)///     use askama::{filters::MaybeSafe, Result, Values};
[253](https://askama.rs#253)///
[254](https://askama.rs#254)///     // Do not actually use this filter! It's an intentionally bad example.
[255](https://askama.rs#255)///     #[askama::filter_fn]
[256](https://askama.rs#256)///     pub fn backdoor<T: std::fmt::Display>(
[257](https://askama.rs#257)///         s: T,
[258](https://askama.rs#258)///         _: &dyn Values,
[259](https://askama.rs#259)///         enable: &bool,
[260](https://askama.rs#260)///     ) -> Result<MaybeSafe<T>> {
[261](https://askama.rs#261)///         Ok(match *enable {
[262](https://askama.rs#262)///             true => MaybeSafe::Safe(s),
[263](https://askama.rs#263)///             false => MaybeSafe::NeedsEscaping(s),
[264](https://askama.rs#264)///         })
[265](https://askama.rs#265)///     }
[266](https://askama.rs#266)/// }
[267](https://askama.rs#267)///
[268](https://askama.rs#268)/// #[derive(askama::Template)]
[269](https://askama.rs#269)/// #[template(
[270](https://askama.rs#270)///     source = "<div class='{{ klass|backdoor(enable_backdoor) }}'></div>",
[271](https://askama.rs#271)///     ext = "html"
[272](https://askama.rs#272)/// )]
[273](https://askama.rs#273)/// struct DivWithBackdoor<'a> {
[274](https://askama.rs#274)///     klass: &'a str,
[275](https://askama.rs#275)///     enable_backdoor: bool,
[276](https://askama.rs#276)/// }
[277](https://askama.rs#277)///
[278](https://askama.rs#278)/// assert_eq!(
[279](https://askama.rs#279)///     DivWithBackdoor { klass: "<script>", enable_backdoor: false }.to_string(),
[280](https://askama.rs#280)///     "<div class='<script>'></div>",
[281](https://askama.rs#281)/// );
[282](https://askama.rs#282)/// assert_eq!(
[283](https://askama.rs#283)///     DivWithBackdoor { klass: "<script>", enable_backdoor: true }.to_string(),
[284](https://askama.rs#284)///     "<div class='<script>'></div>",
[285](https://askama.rs#285)/// );
[286](https://askama.rs#286)/// ```
[287](https://askama.rs#287)pub enum [MaybeSafe](https://askama.rs/askama/filters/enum.MaybeSafe.html)<T> {
[288](https://askama.rs#288)    /// The contained value does not need escaping
[289](https://askama.rs#289)    Safe(T),
[290](https://askama.rs#290)    /// The contained value needs to be escaped
[291](https://askama.rs#291)    NeedsEscaping(T),
[292](https://askama.rs#292)}
[293](https://askama.rs#293)
[294](https://askama.rs#294)const _: () = {

[362](https://askama.rs#362)
[363](https://askama.rs#363)/// Mark the output of a filter as "safe"
[364](https://askama.rs#364)///
[365](https://askama.rs#365)/// This struct can be used as a transparent return type of custom filters that want to mark their
[366](https://askama.rs#366)/// output as "safe" no matter what, i.e. that their output does not need to be escaped.
[367](https://askama.rs#367)///
[368](https://askama.rs#368)/// If the filter is not used as the last element in the filter chain, then any assumption is void.
[369](https://askama.rs#369)/// Let the next filter decide if the output is safe or not.
[370](https://askama.rs#370)///
[371](https://askama.rs#371)/// ## Example
[372](https://askama.rs#372)///
[373](https://askama.rs#373)/// ```rust
[374](https://askama.rs#374)/// mod filters {
[375](https://askama.rs#375)///     use askama::{filters::Safe, Result, Values};
[376](https://askama.rs#376)///
[377](https://askama.rs#377)///     // Do not actually use this filter! It's an intentionally bad example.
[378](https://askama.rs#378)///     #[askama::filter_fn]
[379](https://askama.rs#379)///     pub fn strip_except_apos(s: impl ToString, _: &dyn Values) -> Result<Safe<String>> {
[380](https://askama.rs#380)///         Ok(Safe(s
[381](https://askama.rs#381)///             .to_string()
[382](https://askama.rs#382)///             .chars()
[383](https://askama.rs#383)///             .filter(|c| !matches!(c, '<' | '>' | '"' | '&'))
[384](https://askama.rs#384)///             .collect()
[385](https://askama.rs#385)///         ))
[386](https://askama.rs#386)///     }
[387](https://askama.rs#387)/// }
[388](https://askama.rs#388)///
[389](https://askama.rs#389)/// #[derive(askama::Template)]
[390](https://askama.rs#390)/// #[template(
[391](https://askama.rs#391)///     source = "<div class='{{ klass|strip_except_apos }}'></div>",
[392](https://askama.rs#392)///     ext = "html"
[393](https://askama.rs#393)/// )]
[394](https://askama.rs#394)/// struct DivWithClass<'a> {
[395](https://askama.rs#395)///     klass: &'a str,
[396](https://askama.rs#396)/// }
[397](https://askama.rs#397)///
[398](https://askama.rs#398)/// assert_eq!(
[399](https://askama.rs#399)///     DivWithClass { klass: "<&'lifetime X>" }.to_string(),
[400](https://askama.rs#400)///     "<div class=''lifetime X'></div>",
[401](https://askama.rs#401)/// );
[402](https://askama.rs#402)/// ```
[403](https://askama.rs#403)pub struct [Safe](https://askama.rs/askama/filters/struct.Safe.html)<T>(pub T);
[404](https://askama.rs#404)
[405](https://askama.rs#405)const _: () = {

# MaybeSafe in askama::filters - Rust

Source: https://askama.rs/en/latest/doc/askama/filters/enum.MaybeSafe.html

```
pub enum MaybeSafe<T> {
    Safe(T),
    NeedsEscaping(T),
}
```
## Expand description

Mark the output of a filter as “maybe safe”

This enum can be used as a transparent return type of custom filters that want to mark their output as “safe” depending on some circumstances, i.e. that their output maybe does not need to be escaped.

If the filter is not used as the last element in the filter chain, then any assumption is void. Let the next filter decide if the output is safe or not.

[§](https://askama.rs#example)Example

```
mod filters {
    use askama::{filters::MaybeSafe, Result, Values};
    // Do not actually use this filter! It's an intentionally bad example.
    #[askama::filter_fn]
    pub fn backdoor<T: std::fmt::Display>(
        s: T,
        _: &dyn Values,
        enable: &bool,
    ) -> Result<MaybeSafe<T>> {
        Ok(match *enable {
            true => MaybeSafe::Safe(s),
            false => MaybeSafe::NeedsEscaping(s),
        })
    }
}
#[derive(askama::Template)]
#[template(
    source = "<div class='{{ klass|backdoor(enable_backdoor) }}'></div>",
    ext = "html"
)]
struct DivWithBackdoor<'a> {
    klass: &'a str,
    enable_backdoor: bool,
}
assert_eq!(
    DivWithBackdoor { klass: "<script>", enable_backdoor: false }.to_string(),
    "<div class='<script>'></div>",
);
assert_eq!(
    DivWithBackdoor { klass: "<script>", enable_backdoor: true }.to_string(),
    "<div class='<script>'></div>",
);
```
## Variants[§](https://askama.rs#variants)

[§](https://askama.rs#variant.Safe)

### Safe(T)

The contained value does not need escaping

[§](https://askama.rs#variant.NeedsEscaping)

### NeedsEscaping(T)

The contained value needs to be escaped

# Safe in askama::filters - Rust

Source: https://askama.rs/en/latest/doc/askama/filters/struct.Safe.html

`pub struct Safe<T>(pub T);`## Expand description

Mark the output of a filter as “safe”

This struct can be used as a transparent return type of custom filters that want to mark their output as “safe” no matter what, i.e. that their output does not need to be escaped.

If the filter is not used as the last element in the filter chain, then any assumption is void. Let the next filter decide if the output is safe or not.

[§](https://askama.rs#example)Example

```
mod filters {
    use askama::{filters::Safe, Result, Values};
    // Do not actually use this filter! It's an intentionally bad example.
    #[askama::filter_fn]
    pub fn strip_except_apos(s: impl ToString, _: &dyn Values) -> Result<Safe<String>> {
        Ok(Safe(s
            .to_string()
            .chars()
            .filter(|c| !matches!(c, '<' | '>' | '"' | '&'))
            .collect()
        ))
    }
}
#[derive(askama::Template)]
#[template(
    source = "<div class='{{ klass|strip_except_apos }}'></div>",
    ext = "html"
)]
struct DivWithClass<'a> {
    klass: &'a str,
}
assert_eq!(
    DivWithClass { klass: "<&'lifetime X>" }.to_string(),
    "<div class=''lifetime X'></div>",
);
```
